paper_metadata.title: Practical Meta-Reinforcement Learning of Evolutionary Strategy with Quantum Neural Networks for Stock Trading

experiments.description: Classical meta-reinforcement learning stock-trading experiment using MAML with Natural Evolution Strategies on Consumer Cyclical stock portfolios, including meta-training on 5 portfolios and fast adaptation to one unseen test portfolio.

algorithm.variant: MAML with NES parameter optimization for stock trading
algorithm.convergence_criteria: Trained for 2500 epochs on training portfolios; meta-adaptation on test portfolio for 20 epochs
algorithm.parameter_initialization: Not specified; MAML uses a separate meta-parameter set theta' initialized with the same structure as theta

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Closing prices over a 10-day window are fed as neural-network inputs; outputs are softmax portfolio weights over cash plus stocks
problem_formulation.objective_function: Maximize cumulative portfolio value / logarithmic rate of return over time
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Softmax output enforces portfolio weights summing to 1; cash weight included as first component

problem_instance.description: Portfolio trading over Consumer Cyclical stocks with meta-training on randomly sampled portfolios and evaluation on a fixed unseen portfolio
problem_instance.dataset_name: Yahoo Finance Consumer Cyclical stock data

dataset_specification.date_range: Training data from 1/2/2001 to 1/4/2002; backtest from 1/7/2002 to 6/12/2002
preprocessing: Restrict stocks to price between $0 and $50
Normalize using logarithmic rate of return

classical_preprocessing: Randomly sample portfolios from 60 Consumer Cyclical stocks
Split data into 70% training and 30% testing
classical_postprocessing: Apply softmax to network outputs to obtain portfolio weights
Evaluate by ROI and portfolio value

speedup_claims.factor: 0.01% of original training samples / 20 epochs vs 2500 epochs
speedup_claims.baseline_method: classical training on Consumer Cyclical portfolios
speedup_claims.conditions: meta-adaptation on one unseen portfolio after meta-training
speedup_claims.caveats: This is a reduction in training effort, not a runtime speedup; performance is comparable to buy-and-hold within 0.1% ROI per the abstract.

experiments.description: Classical meta-reinforcement learning stock-trading experiment using CAVIA with NES on Consumer Cyclical stock portfolios, including context-parameter adaptation to one unseen test portfolio.

algorithm.variant: CAVIA with NES parameter optimization for stock trading
algorithm.ansatz: Feedforward neural network with context parameters
algorithm.convergence_criteria: Trained for 2500 epochs on training portfolios; meta-adaptation on test portfolio for 20 epochs

hyperparameters.input_layer_size: doubles due to concatenated context parameters

algorithm.parameter_initialization: Context parameters initialized to 0 in the inner loop; shared parameters initialized with same structure as the classical network

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Closing prices over a 10-day window are fed as inputs; 5 context parameters are concatenated to the input; outputs are softmax portfolio weights
problem_formulation.objective_function: Maximize cumulative portfolio value / logarithmic rate of return over time
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Softmax output enforces portfolio weights summing to 1; cash weight included as first component

problem_instance.description: Portfolio trading over Consumer Cyclical stocks with meta-training on randomly sampled portfolios and evaluation on a fixed unseen portfolio
problem_instance.dataset_name: Yahoo Finance Consumer Cyclical stock data

dataset_specification.date_range: Training data from 1/2/2001 to 1/4/2002; backtest from 1/7/2002 to 6/12/2002
preprocessing: Restrict stocks to price between $0 and $50
Normalize using logarithmic rate of return

classical_preprocessing: Randomly sample portfolios from 60 Consumer Cyclical stocks
Split data into 70% training and 30% testing
classical_postprocessing: Apply softmax to network outputs to obtain portfolio weights
Evaluate by ROI and portfolio value

speedup_claims.factor: 0.01% of original training samples / 20 epochs vs 2500 epochs
speedup_claims.baseline_method: classical training on Consumer Cyclical portfolios
speedup_claims.conditions: meta-adaptation on one unseen portfolio after meta-training
speedup_claims.caveats: This is a reduction in training effort, not a runtime speedup; CAVIA underperformed MAML in ROI and had higher standard deviation.

experiments.description: Quantum meta-reinforcement learning experiment using Q-MAML without beamsplitter gates on a simulated continuous-variable quantum computer for 2-stock portfolios.

algorithm.ansatz: Continuous-variable quantum neural network with rotation, squeezing, rotation, displacement, and Kerr gates
algorithm.convergence_criteria: Trained for 25 epochs on training portfolios; meta-adaptation on test portfolio for 5 epochs

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Each stock closing-price input is encoded into its own wire via a displacement gate; one additional wire is used for cash bias
problem_formulation.objective_function: Maximize cumulative portfolio value / logarithmic rate of return over time
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Softmax applied to measured outputs to produce portfolio weights summing to 1

problem_instance.description: Backtesting stock trading on a 2-asset Consumer Cyclical portfolio using ABC and AKAM
problem_instance.dataset_name: Yahoo Finance Consumer Cyclical stock data

preprocessing: Restrict stocks to price between $0 and $50
Normalize using logarithmic rate of return

classical_preprocessing: Encode each stock on a separate wire with displacement gates
classical_postprocessing: Measure each wire to obtain classical outputs
Evaluate by ROI and portfolio value

speedup_claims.caveats: No runtime or asymptotic speedup claim is made; the paper emphasizes limited simulation scale and reduced training epochs due to computational constraints.
